reference: Runnable expectations use Bash's documented builtin type/help behavior and the loadable's documented help contract. Keyring operation expectations are anchored to the documented Linux keyctl/add_key syscall ABI and the software contract in sol-keyctl.md; no operation result is inferred from candidate output.
coverage: Bash recognizes keyctl as a builtin with PATH empty.
Bash help exposes the documented keyctl synopsis and descriptions.
Deferred: owned anonymous and named session keyring creation.
Deferred: binary payload add, search, print, and update identity.
Deferred: revoke, clear, and key lifecycle error behavior.
Deferred: alias parsing, signed 32-bit serials, and argument boundaries.
Deferred: kernel denial, missing-key, input, and output failure behavior.
exclusions: No keyring syscall was invoked. Session, add, search, print, revoke, and clear cases require a future disposable VM with an owned child keyring or a reviewed closed syscall mock.
No keyutils command-line parity is claimed; actual keyring behavior is not established by Bash metadata cases.
No host keyring, credentials, devices, or system state are used.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Check the documented Bash type -t result for an available builtin while external command lookup is disabled.
Verify the registered synopsis and documented body; Bash may indent static builtin help differently from dynamically loaded help.
cases.script: doc=$(help keyctl) || exit 1; [[ $doc == *"keyctl {session|add|search|print|revoke|clear} ..."* && $doc == *"Small Linux keyring syscall wrapper."* && $doc == *"Verbs: session, add, search, print, revoke, clear."* && $doc == *"add reads at most 1048575 payload bytes; key types may impose smaller limits."* && $doc == *"Names/descriptions: at most 4095 bytes. Serials: signed 32-bit decimal."* ]] || exit 1; printf "documented keyctl metadata\n"

cases.purpose: Deferred operation check for anonymous and named session creation, including serial output and ensuring all later operations are confined to the newly owned ring.
Deferred operation check for byte-exact payload handling, lookup, printing without an added newline, and same-description update identity.
Deferred operation check for revocation, link clearing, and repeated clear behavior on only keys created by the fixture.
Deferred operation check for recognized keyring aliases and signed 32-bit decimal key serial parsing.
Deferred operation check for verb arity, type/description limits, and bounded stdin payload handling.
Deferred operation check for keyring syscall errors and stdin/stdout failures without affecting external keyring state.
